title: Places: spatial splits and features
request: Let DCLab see when places cluster (prices across a city) and test on areas the model has not seen, in the product's engine, with the maps pack running on it.
spec: A spatial part usable by any kind with coordinates: grid cells, distances, neighbourhood counts fitted inside folds, and spatial block cross-validation when places cluster; a check for random splits on spatially autocorrelated data; ties the maps pack to it. Done when a replica with spatial autocorrelation shows the random split's optimism against spatial blocks, and the engine picks blocks for it.
plan: Measure, on the training rows, whether nearby targets are alike (Moran's I) and over what distance (the correlation range).
Let the plan choose blocks of that size, and the validator refuse a random split while places cluster.
Carry the blocks into the Solution and have the engine derive them as the group of every split.
Add a places kind on the maps pack, accepted through the engine on a replica with a district price field.
Review, fix, and show each test fails on the fault it guards.

decisions.decision: Rows in time keep the time split; blocks come before a random split only.
decisions.why: Blocks first dropped the time order even when prices rose 80% over the data, putting later rows in training (DCLAB-R02).

decisions.decision: The notebook export refuses a project split by blocks.
decisions.why: Its split code knows time and group columns only, so it would have scored exactly the random split the package exists to prevent.

decisions.decision: Coordinates not in degrees give an info finding and no blocks.
decisions.why: Metres read as degrees gave a block of 479,328 km, and the Solution then refused the whole adopted plan.

decisions.decision: A random split on clustered places is recorded as a risk by the engine even when no plan set blocks.
decisions.why: The wizard cannot set blocks yet; a person who skips the plan must still be told.

change: dclab_core/spatial.py, dclab_core/analyse.py (_places), dclab_core/plan.py (spatial_block, validate, guard), dclab_core/replicas/city_prices.py, dclab_rnd/core_adapter.py, dclab_rnd/studio/solution.py (SpatialSplit), dclab_rnd/kinds/base.py (default_split), dclab_rnd/studio/engine.py (derived blocks, few-blocks refusal, spatial evidence, data-stage risk), dclab_rnd/studio/export.py (refusal), dclab_rnd/kinds/acceptance.py (the plan's blocks adopted), dclab_rnd/kinds/places.py, tests/test_spatial.py.

findings.defect: Blocks overrode the time split even when the target drifts.
findings.scenario: City prices with a listing date and an 80% rise: F-time warning and F-places warning, plan spatial_block, validate empty, and a planner proposing time refused.
findings.cause: The blocks branch came before the time branches, and the guard refused any other split.
findings.fix: Blocks only when no entity group and no time column; otherwise named as the risk; the guard refuses only a random replacement.
findings.impact: Later rows would have trained a model scored on earlier ones.

findings.defect: The notebook export of a spatial project split at random.
findings.scenario: The places acceptance project exported a notebook with train_test_split and KFold(shuffle) while claiming to reproduce the approved workflow.
findings.cause: The export reads time and group columns only.
findings.fix: The export refuses a spatial project, saying why.

findings.defect: Coordinates not in degrees broke plan adoption, and the antimeridian was ignored.
findings.scenario: UTM metres under lat/lon gave block_km 479328 and the Solution refused the adopted plan; points 10 km apart across 180 degrees were 38,146 km apart.
findings.fix: No blocks unless the values are degrees; longitudes unwrapped when that narrows them.

findings.defect: The product's wizard could not reach blocks, and nothing warned.
findings.scenario: Home, maps pack, accept: the project ran as regression with a time or random split and no warning.
findings.cause: Blocks arrive only by adopting the plan.
findings.fix: The data stage records a risk when places cluster under a random split; the wizard field stays open.

findings.defect: Neighbourhood counts fitted inside folds and distances were not delivered.
findings.scenario: neighbourhood_counts was called only by its unit test.
findings.fix: Stated in the docstring, the changelog and the playbook as open.

findings.defect: Too few blocks failed with sklearn's raw error.
findings.scenario: 30 km blocks on the city gave 4 blocks and 'Cannot have number of splits n_splits=5 greater than the number of groups: 4'.
findings.fix: The engine refuses in words when blocks are fewer than the folds need.

findings.scenario: F-places read on every row, and the advisor guard removed, both passed the tests.
findings.fix: A test that changing rows outside the training partition changes no evidence, and one that the guard refuses a random replacement.

outcome: Built and running in the engine: the plan picks blocks of places, the engine keeps each on one side, and the maps pack reads Supported (places 5/5).
lessons: A new split must take its place among the old rules, not above them: time order and entities still come first.
Every path that reproduces a split (exports included) must know the new split, or refuse.
Check the units of coordinates before turning them into kilometres.
A capability reached only through one path needs a warning on the others.
risks: Later rows in training when time is dropped for blocks.
Exports that reproduce a different split than the engine ran.
